input.task: What does the main heading on the page say?

provenance: M12 gave `run_task` an optional `browser` argument so the eval suite can share one Chromium across cases (11.3s of the fast suite's 67.0s was per-case driver start + launch + close). The harness then passed a browser on EVERY case, which left `browser=None` — the branch the gateway and the CLI, i.e. every real caller, actually take — graded by nothing at all: it could be deleted and the suite would stay 1.000. This case is the one run that refuses the shared browser. Watched red before the case existed by deleting the `if browser is None:` launch block from agent.py: the whole suite stayed green, which is the failure. Watched red with the case present by the same edit: `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'new_context'`, this case alone.

triage.note: the same family as `nav-action-load-event-never-fires`: two code paths do the same job, one of them is exercised by the suite, and a defect in the other survives a green run. It duplicates `tc1-hello-heading` on purpose — cheapest possible run (~0.3s, one extract, no navigation of consequence), because what it grades is the launch, not the extraction.
triage.not_covered: it does not grade browser ISOLATION between shared-browser cases. Each run gets its own BrowserContext, so cookies and storage cannot cross, and every derived figure reproduced across the browser-sharing change on the same 88-case suite — 168 actions, recovery 7/7, mutation 9/11 with 6 recovered / 5 relocated, diagnosis 14/14, 4 replans, before and after (this case then took the suite to 89 cases and 170 actions). But nothing pins isolation itself.
